result.question: Classify the forests of India and describe the distribution and characteristics of the major forest types. (Answer in 150 words)

sentences.text: India's natural vegetation varies with rainfall, temperature, altitude and soil, and its forests are broadly grouped into five types.
Tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests grow on the windward western slopes of the Western Ghats, the north-eastern hills and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
They look green all year, as trees have no fixed season for shedding leaves, and include rosewood, mahogany and ebony.
Tropical deciduous or monsoon forests are the most widespread type, with teak and sal among their main species.
Tropical thorn forests of babool, ber and khejri occur in semi-arid Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab and Haryana.
Montane forests change with altitude, from deciduous forests in the Himalayan foothills to conifers such as deodar and, higher up, alpine pastures.
Temperate forests called sholas occur in the Nilgiri, Anaimalai and Palani hills.
Littoral and swamp forests, including mangroves, are best developed in the Sundarbans and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
As forests face encroachment, sustainable management with local community participation must be strengthened.
